clue.text: Issue complaint after incomplete solution

definitions.note: a verb: to issue or publish something

indicators.note: after places the complaint at the end, behind the shortened solution
incomplete says the word for the solution loses its final letter here

parts.note: brine is a salt solution
gout is an ailment, a medical complaint

explanation.surface: A grumble about an unfinished answer is put out.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring out a book or product is to publish or release it, an idiom for issuing.

clue.text: Bogart's first with a ring for his partner

indicators.note: the first letter of the film star's name is taken

parts.note: to ring someone is to give them a call

explanation.surface: The film star's opening gambit with a wedding ring for his sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: Lauren Bacall, the actress, was Humphrey Bogart's wife and co-star.
explanation.definitionFit: Lauren Bacall married Humphrey Bogart, so she was literally his partner, a specific example.

clue.text: Girl meets boy under Irish cross

indicators.note: in a down answer the girl and boy sit under the Irish abbreviation

parts.note: Rita is a girl's name
Ted is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A girl meets a lad while being looked down on by an angry Irishman.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross as an adjective means annoyed or angry, a common synonym.

clue.text: Studio assistant beginning to eat beef

parts.note: a grip is a film studio stagehand who handles equipment

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A film-set helper starting to tuck into some beef.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef in its slang sense is a complaint or grievance, as is a gripe.

clue.text: Free French article about battle on the Western Front

indicators.note: about means the French article goes around the battle

parts.note: une is the feminine indefinite article in French
Loos was a 1915 First World War battle in northern France

explanation.surface: A free French newspaper article about a First World War battle.
explanation.definitionFit: To unloose is to set loose or release, a verb meaning to free.

clue.text: Jester found by Prince — Shakespearean, as well

parts.note: a wit is a joker or jester
Prince Hal is the young Henry V in Shakespeare

explanation.surface: A fool appears beside a prince in a Shakespeare play, too.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince Hal of Henry IV keeps company with the jesting Falstaff, so the surface fits the plays.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic adverb meaning besides or in addition, used often in Shakespeare's plays.

clue.text: Male surrounded by a vile mob running fast

indicators.note: surrounded by means the male abbreviation sits inside the rearranged letters
running suggests the mob's letters are in disorder, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A man is caught up in a nasty crowd running at speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' puts AVILEMOB in a new order, IMOVABLE, and M goes in to make the answer. 'fast' looks like speed but means firmly fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Fast in the sense of firmly fixed, like a stuck door, means unable to be moved.

clue.text: Spear dropping on speechless brother

indicators.note: dropping means the little word on is removed from the weapon

parts.note: a harpoon is a spear for whaling

explanation.surface: A spear is falling on a silent sibling.
explanation.definitionFit: Harpo Marx, one of the Marx Brothers, never spoke on screen, playing a mute.

clue.text: Non-professional team without a reserve

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the two words go around the letter a

parts.note: lay means amateur or non-clerical, not of a profession
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: An amateur team lacking a spare player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but here carries its old sense of 'outside', so the A is held within.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay something aside is to keep it back for later, a phrase meaning to set in reserve.

clue.text: Scottish historian audible in city

indicators.note: audible means the historian's name is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Thomas Carlyle was a Scottish historian and essayist

explanation.surface: A Scottish historian can be heard in town.
explanation.walkthrough: Carlisle is a city in north-west England near the Scottish border.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral city in Cumbria, England, so an example of a city.

clue.text: Obsequious soldiers following sergeant-major

indicators.note: following means the soldiers come after the sergeant-major

parts.note: an army is a body of soldiers

explanation.surface: Fawning troops trailing their sergeant-major.
explanation.definitionFit: Smarmy means oily and ingratiating, a close synonym for fawning or obsequious.

clue.text: Fiery saint's removing old trees

explanation.surface: A fiery holy man is clearing away ancient woodland.
explanation.definitionFit: Elms are a common genus of large deciduous trees.

clue.text: Gay bishop quitting first place is able to move supply

parts.note: blithe in its old sense means cheerful or gay
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' is read as 'supplely', not 'provisions': the definition means flexible.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithe means flexible and supple, able to bend and move easily.

clue.text: Unconscious learner — one getting clear round

indicators.note: round means the clear word encircles the learner and one

parts.note: obvious means plain or clear
L is the learner-driver plate
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A dazed learner driver, one making a clear lap of the track.
explanation.definitionFit: Oblivious means unaware of one's surroundings, close to unconscious.

clue.text: Fight not started by English PM

parts.note: a battle is a fight

explanation.walkthrough: Clement Attlee was the UK prime minister from 1945 to 1951.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement Attlee was the British prime minister after the Second World War, an example of a PM.

clue.text: Disgusting form of schoolmate not first in class

indicators.note: form of means the letters are rearranged into a new shape
not means the following letter is left out of the fodder
first in means the opening letter of class is used

explanation.surface: A nasty kind of school friend who's never top of the class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' and 'class' look like school words; take C from SCHOOLMATE and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathsome means hateful or repellent, a synonym of disgusting.

clue.text: Quiet vessel expected at Land's End?

parts.note: a sub is a submarine, a vessel
due means expected, as a train is due

indicators.note: End means the last letter of the word land

explanation.surface: A ship is due to arrive at the tip of Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: Land's End is the westernmost point of Cornwall, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Subdued means low-key and restrained, so quiet.

clue.text: Find Laurel and Hardy ultimately weird

parts.note: to unearth is to dig up or find

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of each comedian's name

explanation.surface: Discovering the comedy duo were strange in the end.

clue.text: Nazi embraces country star

parts.note: Rudolf Hess was a leading Nazi
Peru is a South American country

clue.text: Beckett play with cast of aged men

explanation.surface: A Samuel Beckett drama with a cast of old men.
explanation.definitionFit: Endgame is a 1957 play by Samuel Beckett featuring elderly characters.

clue.text: Love having notes written up

parts.note: so and re are two notes of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Love comes with written musical notes.

clue.text: Old magistrates, terribly severe

clue.text: Fruit mostly spheroid — bananas?

clue.text: Useless cover for commencement of military exercises may be abandoned

indicators.note: commencement of means the first letter of military

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercises

clue.text: Blow nose after rolling casks

indicators.note: rolling means the letters of nose are tumbled about

explanation.surface: A punch on the nose after rolling some barrels.

clue.text: Dickensian character who died in French city

definitions.meaning: ... in Oliver Twist is murdered by Bill Sikes
A city in Lorraine, north-east France

explanation.surface: A character from Dickens perished in a city in France.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the murdered character in Oliver Twist and of the capital of Lorraine.

clue.text: Going west in Prufrock's holiday destination?

in means the letters are found within the poem title's word

clue.text: Was party organiser initially methodical or casual?

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of methodical

clue.text: Dirty home was first to be so called

parts.note: a sty is a pigsty, a filthy home
